claude_initial_call: WEAKEST: the end state itself is undefined

audit.primary_source_citation: Gill S, Vasey AE, De Souza A, Baker J, Smith AT, Kohrt HE, Florek M, Gibbs KD Jr, Tate K, Ritchie DS, Negrin RS. "Rapid development of exhaustion and down-regulation of eomesodermin limit the antitumor activity of adoptively transferred murine natural killer cells." Blood. 2012 Jun 14;119(24):5758-68. PMID 22544698; PMCID PMC3382935; DOI 10.1182/blood-2012-03-415364. This is the ORIGIN paper for the named state — its own abstract says "These results provide the first demonstration of NK-cell exhaustion." It is a primary research paper, not a review. (The most-cited secondary framing, Bi & Tian, "NK Cell Exhaustion," Front Immunol 2017;8:760, PMID 28702032 / PMC5487399, is a REVIEW and was explicitly excluded as the primary source under A.1, though it is quoted below as an admission against interest.)

Direct EPMC fullTextXML for PMC3382935 returned 0 bytes; direct curl of the PMC article page returned only a 21 kB JS shell containing no article body; the publisher page (ashpublications.org) returned HTTP 403; the europepmc.org article page rendered no body text. So: Methods READ, but not archivable into refs/ — the verbatim quotes below carry that retrieval caveat and were not re-verified against a locally archived copy. All counter-evidence papers WERE archived in full: /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC7031155.txt (Judge 2020 review), X5_PMC7260004.txt (Judge 2020 JCI), X5_PMC9007500.txt (Hasim 2022, OA_FULLTEXT), X5_PMC7286441.txt (Blank 2019), X5_PMC5487399.txt (Bi & Tian 2017, OA_FULLTEXT), X5_PMC6715389.txt (Merino 2019).
audit.species: Mouse (C57BL/6 and BALB/c donors/recipients; congenic CD45.1; FVB; Rag2-/-Il2rg-/-; NKG2D-/-; DTR-FOXP3-eGFP), plus one xenograft arm using human NK cells in CB.17-SCID recipients bearing human Raji lymphoma. Counter-evidence spans mouse and human.
audit.what_was_measured: In mice, congenically marked CD45.1+ CD3-DX5+ / CD3-NK1.1+ splenic NK cells, DX5-bead-enriched then sorted to >98% purity, were adoptively transferred at 0.5-1.0x10^6 cells/mouse into irradiated CD45.2+ recipients across five models (BALB/c + A20 lymphoma syngeneic; BALB/c + A20 with allogeneic NK; C57BL/6 + Hoxa9-Meis1 AML; subcutaneous tumour with delayed transfer; CB.17-SCID + human Raji with human NK cells). At days 1, 5, 10, 14-17 and 26 post-transfer, donor cells were re-identified by CD45.1 flow cytometry and scored for surface NKG2D / NK1.1 / NKp46 / CD49b, maturation markers CD27 / CD11b / KLRG1, intracellular Eomesodermin and T-bet, IFN-gamma after PMA/ionomycin restimulation, CD107a degranulation, and 51Cr-release cytotoxicity; a forced-Eomes-overexpression arm tested partial rescue. n = 3-5 mice per group per timepoint, 2-3 independent experiments. Critically for this claim: NO inhibitory/checkpoint receptor panel defining a destination state was reported (PD-1 was looked at and reported negative as "data not shown"; TIM-3, LAG-3 and TIGIT were not measured), NO chromatin or DNA-methylation assay was performed, NO clonal or barcode tracking was used, and no antigen-specific stimulus exists for NK cells. The readout is therefore a population-level DECLINE in effector markers and function in traced donor cells over time — a direction of change — not arrival at any independently defined "exhausted NK" cell.
audit.n: 3-5 mice per group per timepoint; 2-3 independent experiments per figure panel (figure-legend language: "at least 3 (A-D) or 2 (E) independent experiments with at least 3 mice per group", with variants of 4 and 5 mice per group). NOT donors or clones — no clonal resolution at all.
audit.controls: Freshly isolated naive splenic NK cells (day-0 input reference); IL-2-activated cultured NK cells; non-tumour-bearing irradiated recipients (isolating tumour exposure from homeostatic proliferation/lymphopenia); transwell cultures to test soluble-factor mediation; NKG2D-/- donor NK cells; Treg-depletion (DTR-FOXP3-eGFP) arm to exclude Treg-mediated suppression; forced Eomes overexpression as a gain-of-function rescue. Congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 marking is the identity control that makes this a transfer observation rather than a snapshot comparison. MISSING controls that bear directly on this claim: no comparator of transferred vs. host-endogenous NK at the same timepoint under identical proliferative load; no clonal/barcode tracking to separate per-cell conversion from differential survival; no independent definition of the end state against which arrival could be scored.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Three alternatives, in increasing order of damage. (1) THE END STATE IS NOT A STATE — the primary alternative. Gill et al. state verbatim: "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology." The destination B is constituted by an analogy, not by an observation. If "exhausted NK" just means "an NK cell whose IFN-gamma/cytotoxicity is lower than an arbitrary comparator (usually autologous blood NK)", then "NK -> exhausted NK" is not a lineage transition at all; it is a restatement of a functional measurement with an arrow drawn through it, and no fate question is being answered. Bi & Tian's own pro-exhaustion review concedes "the transcriptional factors specific for exhausted NK cells are yet to be defined"; Judge/Murphy/Canter state "there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states" and "there remains controversy as to whether NK cells even undergo exhaustion (as opposed to other dysfunction processes), and if so, the phenotypic markers that define an exhausted NK cell." (2) SELECTION, NOT CONVERSION (the canonical alternative, and it fully survives this design). Donor NK cells were transferred as a bulk polyclonal pool into IRRADIATED, lymphopenic hosts and underwent homeostatic proliferation; the paper itself reports that loss of cytotoxicity "progresses with homeostatic proliferation and tumor exposure." Without clonal or barcode tracking, preferential survival and outgrowth of the already-hypofunctional, terminally mature fraction of the input pool (CD27-CD11b+, KLRG1-high) reproduces every observed population-level fall — mean NKG2D, mean Eomes, mean IFN-gamma, mean lysis — with zero individual cells converting. Congenic CD45.1 marking proves the cells are donor-derived; it does not prove they are the same cells that were functional on day 1. Proliferation-coupled decline is exactly what a selection model predicts, so the paper's own kinetic argument cuts against it. (3) TECHNICAL ARTEFACT in the human literature that built the end state after 2012: the flagship marker PD-1 is either not expressed by NK cells at all (Judge 2020) or is physically stolen from tumour cells (Hasim 2022), and enzymatic tumour dissociation with collagenase/dispase is known to cleave lymphocyte surface molecules, so "intratumoural NK have lost their receptors" can be a digestion artefact.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is unusually decisive because it attacks the DEFINITION of B rather than the transition. (a) Judge SJ et al., J Clin Invest 2020;130(6):3051-3068 (PMID 32134744, PMC7260004, archived): stringent multi-platform assessment (flow, qRT-PCR, RNA-seq) of NK cells from primary human tumours, ex vivo culture, and multiple mouse tumour and viral models — human and mouse NK cells "consistently lack PD-1 expression despite the marked upregulation of other activation/regulatory markers, such as TIGIT," in marked contrast to T cells in the same samples. The prototypical exhaustion marker is absent. (Note: this drew an accompanying commentary, J Clin Invest 2020;130(6):2816-2819, PMID 32391808 — the dispute is live, not settled.) (b) Hasim MS et al., Sci Adv 2022;8(15):eabj3286 (PMID 35417234, PMC9007500, archived full text): Pdcd1-/- NK cells co-cultured with leukemia cells STILL stain positive for PD-1; PD-1 on NK surface "rather than being endogenously expressed, was derived entirely from leukemia cells" via SLAM-receptor-dependent trogocytosis; transwell and actinomycin-D controls exclude soluble transfer and de novo transcription; corroborated in patients with clonal plasma cell disorders, where PD-1+ NK cells co-stain for tumour cell markers. A genetic-knockout control showing the marker is stolen, not induced, is about as strong as artefact evidence gets. (c) THE FOUNDING PAPER ITSELF FAILS THE CANONICAL TEST: Gill 2012 reports it "did not demonstrate increased expression of PD-1, as has been shown for exhausted CD8+ T cells (data not shown)" — the single defining marker of the state it was naming was negative, and was consigned to data not shown. (d) Ndhlovu LC et al., Blood 2012 (PMID 22383801, PMC3335380): TIM-3 "marks human natural killer cell MATURATION" — it is constitutively expressed on healthy mature NK cells, so its later use as an "NK exhaustion marker" (da Silva 2014) is circular. (e) LABEL INSTABILITY WITHIN SINGLE GROUPS: Ardolino et al. classify intratumoural mouse NK cells as "anergic" and reverse it with systemic IL-12/IL-18, while Hsu et al. from the same group describe the same models as PD-1+; Alvarez M et al., JCI Insight 2019 (PMID 31211693) title the state "NK cell exhaustion" while the mechanism they report is the DNA DAMAGE REPAIR pathway — which under T-cell taxonomy is SENESCENCE, not exhaustion. The same cells get three different end-state names. (f) TOX DISANALOGY: in T cells TOX transcriptionally and epigenetically ENFORCES exhaustion (Khan/Alfei/Scott 2019, all cited in Blank 2019). In NK cells TOX is a LINEAGE-SPECIFICATION factor required for the cells to exist — Aliahmad P et al., Nat Immunol 2010 (PMID 20818394), "Shared dependence on the DNA-binding factor TOX for the development of lymphoid tissue-inducer cell and NK cell lineages"; Seehus et al. 2015 (PMID 25915732), TOX-dependent common ILC progenitor. The defining epigenetic driver of the borrowed concept has an incompatible job in the borrowing cell type. (g) NO ANTIGEN RECEPTOR: criterion 1 of the T-cell definition (chronic antigen stimulation through a clonotypic TCR) has no NK counterpart. The closest available substitute, Merino A et al., J Clin Invest 2019;129(9):3770-3785 (PMID 31211698), had to use plate-bound agonistic anti-NKG2C + IL-15 in vitro on human adaptive NK cells — and its own title says "dysfunction and epigenetic reprograming", NOT exhaustion. (h) SEARCHED-AND-NOT-FOUND (G3): I ran five distinct searches for a formal 2019-2024 consensus or nomenclature statement on NK exhaustion or NK dysfunction terminology and located NONE. The nearest thing is the Judge/Murphy/Canter single-group review, not a multi-author consensus. This is a searched negative, NOT a claim that none exists. By contrast the T-cell field's consensus paper was found immediately on the first attempt (Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'", Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19(11):665-674, PMID 31570879, PMC7286441, archived).
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCIES. (1) Clinical: the entire NK-directed checkpoint-blockade rationale — monalizumab (anti-NKG2A) and tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) are developed on the premise that a reversible "exhausted NK" state exists and is the thing being reversed; Judge 2020 lists trials already enrolling on the NK-PD-1 premise specifically (NCT03958097, NCT03815084, NCT03937895). If the end state is only a functional decrement rather than an enforced program, "reinvigoration" has no defined target and the biomarker used for patient selection (checkpoint-receptor positivity on NK) is measuring maturation or trogocytosed protein. (2) Dosing schedules for IL-15 agonists: Felices M et al., JCI Insight 2018;3(3):e96219 (PMID 29415897, PMC5821201), "Continuous treatment with IL-15 exhausts human NK cells via a metabolic defect", is the direct justification for intermittent rather than continuous IL-15/N-803 dosing of adoptively transferred NK products. (3) WITHIN THIS SCREEN: X5 sits directly upstream of R2 ("Tumour NK dysfunction reversible vs fixed") — R2 is unanswerable as posed if there is no defined state whose reversibility can be scored; a reversibility experiment needs a B to revert FROM. X5 also underwrites X2 ("Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK") and supplies the interpretive frame for X4's ENTPD1+ "effector/exhausted" end state and for T4 (NK -> ILC1), where "exhausted" and "converted" are competing labels for the same intratumoural hypofunctional cells. (4) Also load-bearing for CAR-NK product-release criteria, where "exhaustion markers" are used as a QC readout on manufactured cells with no validated definition behind them.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CONFIRMED on substance, OVERTURNED on grade — and the two point in opposite directions, which is the actual finding. CONFIRMED: the end state genuinely is undefined, and the evidence for that is stronger than the initial call assumed. It is not merely that no one has gotten around to defining it; the founding paper defines it by explicit admission of analogy ("We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology"), the field's own flagship pro-exhaustion review concedes the transcription factors "are yet to be defined", the leading critique states flatly that "there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states", and a targeted search found no consensus/nomenclature paper of the kind the T-cell field produced in 2019. Applying the T-cell criteria from Blank 2019 (RULE G4), NK "exhaustion" satisfies NONE of them with direct evidence: no clonotypic antigen receptor, so "chronic antigen stimulation" has no counterpart; no demonstrated TCF1+ progenitor -> TCF1- terminal hierarchy; TOX is a developmental requirement in NK cells rather than an exhaustion enforcer; and it is explicitly NOT separated from anergy or senescence — Judge 2020 says the states "become blurred", and Alvarez 2019 labels a DNA-damage-response phenotype "exhaustion" when that is senescence under the T-cell taxonomy. OVERTURNED: "WEAKEST" is wrong as an evidence-design grade, and the initial call would have mis-ranked this row. The founding primary source is NOT marker similarity, an in vitro culture, or a trajectory — it is a congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 adoptive-transfer experiment with longitudinal re-identification of the traced input population across five tumour models, tumour-free controls, a soluble-factor transwell control, a Treg-depletion control, and a gain-of-function Eomes rescue. That is an OBS_TRANSFER design, methodologically stronger than several rows this screen grades ABOVE X5: stronger than S1 (pseudotime only, INF_TRAJECTORY), T3 (in vitro only), T5 (in vitro), X3 and S2 (phenotypic similarity), and X4 (snRNA/snATAC trajectory). So X5 is not the weakest row in the screen on evidence class; it is roughly on par with D2 and T2. THE CORRECTED CHARACTERISATION: X5's defect is SEMANTIC, not METHODOLOGICAL. A competent in vivo transfer experiment was run, and it points at a destination that does not exist. That is a different and more interesting failure mode than "weak evidence", and it should be recorded as its own category rather than collapsed into the bottom of an evidence-quality ranking — because more data of the same kind cannot fix it. No adoptive transfer, parabiosis, barcode or fate-map can establish "A becomes B" while B is constituted by analogy to a different cell type. One further caveat that cuts the other way and is NOT in the initial call: even the strong OBS_TRANSFER design does not exclude the canonical selection alternative, because transfer was bulk and polyclonal into irradiated lymphopenic hosts and decline tracked with homeostatic proliferation — so the row also fails to exclude "a pre-existing hypofunctional subset outgrew the rest."
audit.methods_quote: Gill 2012 (recovered via WebFetch rendering of PMC3382935; consistent across two independent passes, NOT verifiable against the locally archived abstract-only file): (1) "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology." (2) On the canonical marker: the authors "did not demonstrate increased expression of PD-1, as has been shown for exhausted CD8+ T cells (data not shown)." (3) Sample size, figure-legend language: "Results are representative of at least 3 (A-D) or 2 (E) independent experiments with at least 3 mice per group." (4) Purification: "NK cells were isolated from splenocytes...positively selected using DX5 magnetic beads...sorted for CD3-DX5+ or CD3-NK1.1+ using...cell sorter to > 98% purity." — VERIFIED VERBATIM from locally archived files: Judge/Murphy/Canter 2020, /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC7031155.txt line 27: "different states of NK dysfunction, such as anergy and exhaustion, become blurred because there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states... there remains controversy as to whether NK cells even undergo exhaustion (as opposed to other dysfunction processes), and if so, the phenotypic markers that define an exhausted NK cell." Bi & Tian 2017, /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC5487399.txt line 62: "Although the transcriptional factors specific for exhausted NK cells are yet to be defined..." Hasim 2022, /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC9007500.txt: "PD-1 on the surface of NK cells, rather than being endogenously expressed, was derived entirely from leukemia cells in a SLAM receptor-dependent fashion." Judge 2020 JCI, /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC7260004.txt: "human and mouse NK cells consistently lack PD-1 expression despite the marked upregulation of other activation/regulatory markers, such as TIGIT."
audit.notes: RULE G4 VERDICT (the hint flagged this as critical): NK "exhaustion" fails every explicit criterion of the T-cell field it borrowed the word from. Blank et al. 2019 (PMID 31570879) is itself a Viewpoint in which 18 experts give differing definitions "ranging from complete lack of effector function to altered functionality", so the source concept is not monolithic — but it does converge on four testable anchors: chronic antigen stimulation, hierarchical progressive functional loss, a TCF1+ self-renewing progenitor feeding a TCF1- terminal population, and TOX-driven epigenetic enforcement distinguishing exhaustion from anergy and senescence. NK cells have no clonotypic antigen receptor (anchor 1 undefined by construction); no NK progenitor-to-terminal exhaustion hierarchy has been demonstrated; TOX in NK cells is a developmental lineage factor (Aliahmad 2010, PMID 20818394) not an exhaustion enforcer; and the anergy/senescence boundary is explicitly unresolved (Judge 2020). The single closest NK study, Merino 2019 (PMID 31211698), is in vitro plate-bound anti-NKG2C + IL-15 on human adaptive NK cells and titles its own finding "dysfunction", not exhaustion. G3 COMPLIANCE: 23 distinct searches were run and read (listed in searches_run). The absence of an NK-exhaustion consensus/nomenclature paper is a SEARCHED negative across five differently-phrased attempts, not an assertion of non-existence; if such a statement exists it is not surfacing under PubMed/EPMC queries for consensus, nomenclature, criteria, misnomer, or critical-appraisal phrasings. Note that the lit.py EPMC backend degrades badly on long natural-language queries (returns conference abstract books); boolean/author-title queries were required. NO HINTED CITATION WAS FOUND TO BE FABRICATED: Wherry, Sharpe, Speiser, Blank consensus on nomenclature = confirmed real and located (PMID 31570879); the 2019-2024 critique literature arguing NK dysfunction is not exhaustion = located, but it is a review (PMID 32117816) plus a primary data paper (PMID 32134744) from one group (Murphy/Canter, UC Davis), not a consensus statement — the hint's framing of "consensus/nomenclature papers" for the NK side overstates what exists. RECOMMENDED ROW DISPOSITION: X5 should be moved out of the evidence-quality ranking entirely and recorded as UNGRADEABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION (destination undefined), with a footnote that its primary source is an OBS_TRANSFER design. Ranking it "weakest" implies that better data would settle it; it would not. adv.challenge_reason:
I re-ran `lit.py methods 22544698 --tag X5` (STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY, confirming the archival limit) and independently re-recovered the Methods by WebFetch of PMC3382935 on two fresh prompts. The auditor's factual description of the design is CORRECT and reproducible: C57BL/6 / BALB/c / FVB / CB.17-SCID; CD45.1 donors into CD45.2 recipients; splenocytes DX5-bead-selected then sorted CD3-DX5+ or CD3-NK1.1+ to ">98% purity"; 0.5-1.0x10^6 cells i.v. tail vein; lethal irradiation "800 rad in divided doses" (BALB/c) and "960 rad in divided doses" (B6); serial timepoints; figure legends "at least 3 (A-D) or 2 (E) independent experiments with at least 3 mice per group", plus "n = 4 per group", "4 to 5 mice per group", "composite of 3 independent experiments with a total of 13 to 14 mice per group". So no OBS_* class was invented, and there is NO stronger class to upgrade to: the Eomes arm is a gain-of-function rescue (not fate-mapping), NKG2D-/- donors are genetic but not lineage-tracing, and there is no Cre-lox fate map, no barcode, no parabiosis.

I nevertheless DOWNGRADE, on two grounds, one of which is new empirical evidence rather than semantics.

(1) NEW METHODS FACT THE AUDITOR MISSED — CFSE, in both directions. Gill did run division tracking: "CFSE-labeled C57BL6 NK cells were injected into Rag2-/-gc-/- recipients alone or with 5 x 10^6 A20 tumor cells and sorted into CFSE high (unproliferated) or CFSE low (proliferated) populations." This cuts BOTH ways and the auditor got it wrong in one direction and missed the other. Against the auditor: its claim that "proliferation-coupled decline is exactly what a selection model predicts, so the paper's own kinetic argument cuts against it" is overstated — Gill reports IFN-g loss occurs "without relation to proliferation or tumor burden", and that "proliferating NK cells were no more, and possibly less cytotoxic than nonproliferating cells" (n.s.). That partly excludes the differential-OUTGROWTH form of selection, which the auditor asserted was fully intact. Against the paper: CFSE tracks division, not clonal identity, so differential SURVIVAL of a pre-existing hypofunctional fraction within 24-72h needs no division and remains unexcluded; and no absolute-recovery/input-output accounting is reported.

(2) THE DECISIVE GROUND — the measured axis is a demonstrated-REVERSIBLE tuning parameter, so a decline along it is a kinetic measurement, not the observation of arrival at a state. Elliott JM, Wahle JA, Yokoyama WM, J Exp Med 2010;207:2073-2079 (PMID 20819924, PMC2947074, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC2947074.txt, OA_FULLTEXT) is the mirror-image experiment in the same system: CFSE-labelled splenic NK adoptive transfer, IFN-g-after-crosslinking and CD107a readouts, mouse spleen. Hyporesponsive beta2m-/- NK cells transferred into WT hosts "produced IFN-g at a level equivalent to that of host WT NK cells"; "donor NK cells gained function at WT levels by day 4 after transfer and that their phenotype was stable thereafter"; and critically "donor beta2m-/- NK cells did not proliferate after residence in WT hosts, as indicated by a lack of CFSE dilution". Conclusion: "the unlicensed phenotype is not fixed in apparently mature peripheral NK cells" and "NK cell function in respect to host MHC environment is more plastic than originally anticipated". Elliott's design is BETTER controlled than Gill's on the exact points Gill is weak: transfer "was performed without host irradiation and subset depletion, thereby minimizing the impact of experimental manipulation", and it carries the within-recipient host-NK comparator at the same timepoint that Gill lacks; and the gain-of-function is receptor-restricted (Ly49C+ but not Ly49C-, P=0.02), an internal specificity control no selection/outgrowth model can produce in the absence of division.

So mature peripheral NK effector capacity moves UP on the same days-scale, division-independently, that Gill's moves DOWN, in the same assay system. An adoptive transfer that measures a bidirectional, division-independent rheostat has observed a rate and direction of change in a traced population — INF_KINETIC — not a transition to a defined destination. OBS_TRANSFER remains genuinely present in evidence_types_all, but it establishes DONOR PROVENANCE only; it does not attach to "A becomes B" because nothing in the design identifies a B (no chromatin or DNA-methylation assay; PD-1 explicitly negative and consigned to "data not shown"; TIM-3/LAG-3/TIGIT not measured; no clonal resolution). Gill's own fixity test is a single unshown in vitro line — "Cytotoxic function was not regained after a further 5 days in culture without tumor (data not shown)" — which the auditor also missed, and which conflicts with Elliott's positive in vivo reversibility.

I therefore UPHOLD the auditor's substantive verdict (the destination is undefined) but reject its evidence-grade defence of X5 as "methodologically stronger than several rows this screen grades above it". Recorded correctly, this is INF_KINETIC on an axis known to be reversible, decorated with an OBS_TRANSFER provenance control.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_KINETIC (population-mean decline over time in a congenically traced donor pool, measured along a demonstrated-reversible tuning axis). Full set present, in descending design weight: OBS_TRANSFER (provenance only — CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic re-identification proves donor origin, not arrival at a destination state), INF_KINETIC (the actual claim-bearing readout), INF_MARKER (the destination label is assigned by analogy to CD8 exhaustion — verbatim: "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology"), INF_INVITRO (IL-2-expanded murine NK arms; human NK "expanded using rhIL-15 25 ng/mL for 17 days"; the negative reversibility test was in vitro and unshown). Not present and not creditable: OBS_DIRECT, OBS_GENETIC (Eomes overexpression is rescue, not lineage tracing), INF_TRAJECTORY.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
SIX items the auditor did not have; the first two are the important ones, and both are IN VIVO MOUSE ADOPTIVE TRANSFER — i.e. they beat Gill at its own design, which the auditor's human-marker-artefact case (Judge/Hasim) does not.

(1) REVERSIBILITY, SAME METHOD, OPPOSITE DIRECTION — Elliott JM, Wahle JA, Yokoyama WM. J Exp Med 2010;207(10):2073-2079. PMID 20819924, PMC2947074, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC2947074.txt. Quoted in full in challenge_reason. Hyporesponsive mature splenic NK regain full IFN-g and degranulation within ~72h-4d of transfer, WITHOUT CFSE dilution, stably, receptor-restricted, in NON-irradiated hosts with a within-recipient host comparator. If NK effector capacity is a bidirectional environment-set rheostat on a 4-day timescale, then Gill's downward move is re-tuning, and "exhausted NK" is a reading on a dial, not a terminus.

(2) FAILED REPLICATION OF THE KINETIC CLAIM, SAME YEAR, SAME DESIGN — Ni J, Miller M, Stojanovic A, Garbi N, Cerwenka A. "Sustained effector function of IL-12/15/18-preactivated NK cells against established tumors." J Exp Med 2012;209(13):2351-2365. PMID 23209317, PMC3526364, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC3526364.txt (OA_FULLTEXT). CD45.1 NK into CD45.2 tumour-bearing IRRADIATED (5 Gy) hosts, CFSE, days 4 / 11 / 90. Gill's central kinetic claim is that loss of cytotoxicity "progresses with homeostatic proliferation and tumor exposure" — i.e. proliferation under lymphopenia plus tumour is the exhausting stimulus. Ni applied a MAXIMAL dose of exactly that stimulus: ">95% of IL-12/15/18-preactivated NK cells had proliferated with more than eight daughter generations in spleen" by day 4, in irradiated tumour-bearing mice. Those cells did not decline — they "persist for at least 3 mo", and "six times more IFN-g-expressing transferred IL-12/15/18-preactivated NK cells were observed in irradiated compared with nonirradiated hosts", with granzyme B and perforin also higher in irradiated hosts. Whether transferred NK decline or improve is therefore set by the INPUT cell state (naive/IL-2 vs IL-12/15/18), not by an intrinsic exhaustion program engaged by transfer. That is the input-composition alternative, demonstrated prospectively.

(3) THE CANONICAL "PRE-EXISTING HYPOFUNCTIONAL SUBSET" IS A BASELINE FACT OF NK BIOLOGY, NOT A HYPOTHESIS — Anfossi N et al., "Human NK cell education by inhibitory receptors for MHC class I," Immunity 2006;25:331-342, PMID 16901727; Joncker NT et al., "NK cell responsiveness is tuned commensurate with the number of inhibitory receptors for self-MHC class I: the rheostat model," J Immunol 2009, PMID 19342631. A large fraction of NK cells in every healthy mouse and human is constitutively hyporesponsive by education status, before any tumour or transfer. Gill transferred BULK polyclonal NK, so hypofunctional cells were a substantial part of the day-0 input. This is the input-heterogeneity precondition the selection alternative needs, and it is established, not speculative.

(4) DIFFERENTIAL EXPANSION OF THE HYPOFUNCTIONAL FRACTION IS DOCUMENTED IN VIVO — AND GILL CITES IT — Orr MT, Murphy WJ, Lanier LL. "'Unlicensed' natural killer cells dominate the response to cytomegalovirus infection." Nat Immunol 2010;11:321-327, PMID 20190757 (reference 44 of Gill 2012). Hyporesponsive unlicensed NK preferentially dominate an in vivo response. Combined with Jamieson AM et al., J Immunol 2004;172:864-870, PMID 14707057 (NK turnover under lymphopenia, also cited by Gill), the selection route has direct in vivo support from Gill's own reference list.

(5) THE HUMAN "DYSFUNCTIONAL NK" PHENOTYPE WAS FIRST DESCRIBED AS AN EXPANDED PRE-EXISTING SUBSET — Mavilio D et al., "Characterization of CD56-/CD16+ natural killer (NK) cells: a highly dysfunctional NK subset EXPANDED in HIV-infected viremic individuals," PNAS 2005, PMID 15699323. The title states the alternative. This predates Gill by seven years and frames the identical observation (hypofunctional NK accumulate in chronic disease) as subset expansion, not conversion.

(6) LABEL INSTABILITY, STRONGEST EXAMPLE — Schlums H et al., Immunity 2015;42:443-456, PMID 25786176 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC4612277.txt, abstract only). HCMV-driven adaptive NK subsets show "altered cytokine responsiveness ... linked to reduced expression of the transcription factor PLZF" and "significantly reduced functional responses", with promoter DNA hypermethylation. Same surface reading as "exhaustion" (NCR-low, poor cytokine response), opposite label (adaptive/memory), and these cells have SUPERIOR ADCC. An epigenetically defined NK state does exist in the literature — it is just not the one called exhausted.

(7) DOWNSTREAM COUNTER-DATA — Zhang Q et al., Nat Immunol 2018;19:723-732, PMID 29915296, "Blockade of the checkpoint receptor TIGIT prevents NK cell exhaustion and elicits potent anti-tumor immunity" is the paper that converted the X5 frame into a therapeutic hypothesis; the tiragolumab programme built on it missed primary endpoints in SKYSCRAPER-01 (NSCLC) and SKYSCRAPER-02 (SCLC) and in liver, oesophageal and head-and-neck trials, and Roche discontinued tiragolumab in July 2025 after ~5,000 patients. Also Roe K, Immunology 2022, PMID 35266556, "NK-cell exhaustion, B-cell exhaustion and T-cell exhaustion - the differences and similarities" (secondary; not usable as primary source).

G3 NOTE: I ran an independent, differently-phrased search for a 2023-2026 NK-state nomenclature/guidelines statement ("natural killer cell states nomenclature guidelines recommendations reporting 2023 2024 2025 2026") and returned NOTHING, independently confirming the auditor's searched negative from a query it did not use. This is SEARCHED-AND-NOT-FOUND, not non-existence.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
I searched the CD8 T cell field (the home field of "exhaustion") and the ILC field. The T cell field established exhaustion as a genuine lineage state via THREE methodological anchors. NK "exhaustion" has none of them, and on the one anchor that has been directly tested in NK cells the answer came back NEGATIVE.

ANCHOR 1 — EPIGENETIC FIXITY IS THE CRITERION THAT SEPARATES EXHAUSTION FROM REVERSIBLE TUNING. Sen DR et al., "The epigenetic landscape of T cell exhaustion," Science 2016, PMID 27789799, defined exhaustion-specific enhancers distinct from effector and memory states; Pauken KE et al., "Epigenetic stability of exhausted T cells limits durability of reinvigoration by PD-1 blockade," Science 2016, PMID 27789795, showed the chromatin state is NOT remodelled by checkpoint blockade, which is why reinvigoration is transient. This is precisely what makes "T cell becomes exhausted T cell" a lineage claim rather than a description of low function. Gill 2012 performed NO chromatin or DNA-methylation assay. Worse, the direct NK test of fixity exists and is negative: Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) shows mature NK hyporesponsiveness reverses completely in ~4 days in vivo without division. Under the T cell field's own criterion, that is tuning/anergy, not exhaustion.

ANCHOR 2 — THE PRECURSOR-PRODUCT HIERARCHY WAS ESTABLISHED BY SORTED-SUBSET ADOPTIVE TRANSFER, NOT BULK TRANSFER. Im SJ et al., Nature 2016, PMID 27501248; Utzschneider DT et al., Immunity 2016, PMID 27533016; Miller BC et al., Nat Immunol 2019, PMID 30778252; Beltra JC et al., "Developmental Relationships of Four Exhausted CD8+ T Cell Subsets...", Immunity 2020, PMID 32396847. In every case a candidate PROGENITOR (TCF1+/PD-1+) was sorted, transferred, and shown to give rise to the candidate TERMINAL product. That is the experiment that licenses an arrow. Gill transferred BULK polyclonal NK and re-read the same pool — it never sorted a candidate precursor state and showed it yields a candidate product state. This is the decisive G4 finding: the missing experiment is not exotic, it is the same adoptive-transfer technique Gill already had in hand, and no one has run it for NK "exhaustion". Note this also means my DOWNGRADE is not merely semantic — the T cell field draws exactly this line between bulk-population kinetics and a demonstrated lineage step.

ANCHOR 3 — A TF THAT ENFORCES THE STATE AND IS DISPENSABLE FOR DEVELOPMENT. Khan O et al., "TOX transcriptionally and epigenetically programs CD8+ T cell exhaustion," Nature 2019, PMID 31207603 (with Scott/Alfei companions). In NK cells TOX is a lineage-specification requirement — Aliahmad P et al., Nat Immunol 2010, PMID 20818394 — so the borrowed concept's defining enforcer has an incompatible job in the borrowing lineage. This confirms the auditor's point; the auditor had this one right.

CONSENSUS: Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'," Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19:665-674, PMID 31570879 — confirmed real and located. Its four anchors (chronic antigen stimulation through a clonotypic receptor; hierarchical progressive functional loss; TCF1+ progenitor to TCF1- terminal hierarchy; TOX-driven epigenetic enforcement separating exhaustion from anergy and senescence) are satisfied by NK exhaustion with direct evidence in ZERO cases. Anchor 1 is undefined by construction (no clonotypic receptor); Anchor 2 is untested in NK; Anchor 3 is untested in NK; Anchor 4 is inverted in NK.

ILC FIELD: the structurally analogous problem (a lineage whose states are defined by plasticity and marker overlap) was answered there with a formal nomenclature — Vivier E et al., "Innate Lymphoid Cells: 10 Years On," Cell 2018;174:1054-1066, PMID 30142344. No equivalent exists for NK dysfunction states; my independent search returned none (see G3 note).

TRM/PARABIOSIS: NOT_SEARCHED. Recruitment-versus-residency is not the mechanism X5 invokes; that methodology bears on other rows in this screen (T-series), not on this one.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
HIGH is correct, but the auditor's dependency set is half wrong and I replace it with a concrete, dated, checkable one.

REJECTED FROM THE AUDITOR'S LIST: monalizumab (anti-NKG2A) is NOT load-bearing on X5. Its rationale is NKG2A-HLA-E receptor-ligand biology, which stands or falls independently of whether an "exhausted NK state" exists — blocking an inhibitory receptor does not require the cell to be in a named program. Citing it inflates the dependency count.

THE CONCRETE, NAMED DEPENDENCY I WOULD PUT IN THE ROW INSTEAD — Zhang Q, Bi J, Zheng X, et al. "Blockade of the checkpoint receptor TIGIT prevents NK cell exhaustion and elicits potent anti-tumor immunity." Nat Immunol 2018;19(7):723-732, PMID 29915296. This is the specific derivative paper that took X5's frame — an NK cell that BECOMES exhausted and can therefore be PREVENTED from doing so — and converted it into a therapeutic hypothesis, in its title. The anti-TIGIT clinical programme built on that hypothesis then failed comprehensively: tiragolumab missed primary endpoints in SKYSCRAPER-01 (PD-L1-high NSCLC, n=534) and SKYSCRAPER-02 (SCLC), and in liver, oesophageal and head-and-neck trials; Roche discontinued tiragolumab in July 2025 after roughly 5,000 patients enrolled across the programme. That is a dated, costed, publicly documented downstream consequence — exactly the kind of dependency this field is HIGH on. Note carefully what this does and does not show: the failures do not prove X5 false, and TIGIT blockade also targets CD8 T cells. But it is the clearest available demonstration that the "reversible exhausted NK state" frame was used to justify a very large clinical bet, which is what load-bearing means. Corroborating: a 2023 iScience report explicitly titled to the effect that TIGIT "does not define NK cell dysfunction in glioblastoma" (located by WebSearch; PMID not resolved by my searches — flagged as UNVERIFIED, do not cite without checking).

SECOND CONCRETE DEPENDENCY (auditor's, verified and kept) — Felices M et al., "Continuous treatment with IL-15 exhausts human NK cells via a metabolic defect," JCI Insight 2018;3(3):e96219, PMID 29415897 (PMID independently confirmed). This is the stated justification for INTERMITTENT rather than continuous IL-15/N-803 dosing of adoptively transferred NK products — a live dosing-schedule decision derived from the exhaustion frame.

THIRD — WITHIN-SCREEN, and this is the strongest reason HIGH survives the downgrade. R2 ("Tumour NK dysfunction reversible vs fixed") is not merely unanswerable-as-posed; my Elliott 2010 finding partly ANSWERS it in the direction that dissolves X5, since mature NK hyporesponsiveness demonstrably reverses in ~4 days in vivo without division. X5 also supplies the interpretive frame for X2, for X4's ENTPD1+ "effector/exhausted" end state, and for T4 (NK -> ILC1), where "exhausted" and "converted" compete as labels for the same intratumoural hypofunctional cells — and note Gao 2017 (PMID 28759001) carries an Author Correction (PMID 38514890), which the screen should check before leaning on T4.

FOURTH — CAR-NK product-release criteria using "exhaustion markers" as QC on manufactured cells. I did not verify a specific release specification document, so this is retained at the auditor's assertion level: NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.
adv.better_primary_source:
KEEP PMID 22544698 (Gill et al., Blood 2012;119:5758-68, PMC3382935, DOI 10.1182/blood-2012-03-415364) as the primary source for the NAMED state. I verified its self-nomination in the recovered text — "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology" — and a WebSearch for pre-2012 primary use of the term surfaced no earlier primary research paper claiming it. The auditor's A.1 exclusion of Bi & Tian 2017 (PMID 28702032) as a review is correct.

BUT THE ROW SHOULD RECORD A CORRECTION: the primary source for the PHENOMENON predates the label by seven years, and those earlier primaries interpret the identical readout the opposite way. Gill's flagship readout is NKG2D downmodulation with loss of cytotoxicity in vivo. That was first shown, in vivo, by Oppenheim DE et al., "Sustained localized expression of ligand for the activating NKG2D receptor impairs natural cytotoxicity in vivo and reduces tumor immunosurveillance," Nat Immunol 2005;6:928-937, PMID 16116470, and mechanistically extended by Coudert JD, Scarpellino L, Gros F, Vivier E, Held W, "Sustained NKG2D engagement induces cross-tolerance of multiple distinct NK cell activation pathways," Blood 2008;111:3571-3578, PMID 18198346. Both are cited BY Gill (references 45 and 46 of its own reference list, visible in the archived PubMed record at /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC3382935.txt), and both frame the phenomenon as ligand-driven receptor downmodulation and reversible TOLERANCE/CROSS-TOLERANCE, not as a differentiation endpoint. On the human side the earlier primary is Mavilio D et al., PNAS 2005, PMID 15699323, whose title states the competing model outright: a dysfunctional NK subset "EXPANDED in HIV-infected viremic individuals".

So the accurate provenance line for X5 is: Gill 2012 renamed, by explicit analogy, a phenomenon whose primary in vivo description (Oppenheim 2005; Coudert 2008) and primary human description (Mavilio 2005) already existed under interpretations — reversible receptor tolerance, and expansion of a pre-existing subset — that are precisely the two alternatives this screen is supposed to test the claim against.

FULLTEXT CAVEAT, unchanged and independently reproduced: Blood 2012 is outside the EPMC OA subset; `lit.py methods 22544698` returns ABSTRACT_ONLY and refs/X5_PMC3382935.txt is abstract + reference list only (12 kB). I recovered Methods by WebFetch of the PMC rendering across two fresh prompts in a separate session from the original audit, obtaining content that was mutually consistent AND that added material the original audit missed (CFSE-high/CFSE-low sorting; the negative in vitro reversibility line; 800/960 rad doses; exact strain list). Cross-session reproducibility raises confidence in these quotes, but they remain NOT ARCHIVABLE into refs/ and should carry that flag. By contrast, both of my decisive counter-evidence papers ARE archived in full: /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC2947074.txt (Elliott 2010) and /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC3526364.txt (Ni 2012).
